learning_outcomes.text: Basic knowledge of production and manufacturing systems.
Applied knowledge of manufacturing systems and processes, metrology, and quality control.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, abilities, and skills in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to apply quality principles and methods.
Identify different manufacturing processes and systems, including advantages and disadvantages, and potential defects in their application.

Select the most appropriate manufacturing processes based on knowledge of their capabilities and limitations and according to the technological, technical, and economic demands of both product and market.
Interpret metrological control guidelines used to ensure product and process quality.
Recognize and apply the basic considerations for configuring a process sheet.
Know quality tools and be able to integrate manufacturing and measurement functions into them.

syllabus_topics: Concept of manufacturing and general classification of manufacturing processes.
Mechanics of cutting and machining economy
Manufacturing Systems. Tooling. Machine tool programming.
Industrial inspection and metrology. Measurement methods systems
Geometric measurement with conventional systems and with three-coordinate measuring systems.
Quality tools applied to machining processes: Design of Experiments, Control Charts, Process Capability.
teaching_methods: Practical sessions (using specialized software and workshop/metrology lab equipment)

assessment_methods.method: Evaluation of practical sessions on metrology and quality tools (reports)
Control on Metrology / Quality tools (global test)
Teamwork on component machining (report, CAM files, presentation)

assessment_rules: The final grade for continuous assessment is calculated as: 0.15 * practical reports grade + 0.3 * Metrology/Quality control grade + 0.3 * Machining teamwork grade + 0.25 * Machining control grade. Minimum grades are required for each component: 4/10 for practical reports, 4/10 for the Metrology/Quality control exam part and 3/10 for its problem part, 5/10 for machining teamwork, and 4/10 for machining control. Students failing continuous assessment minimums will take a global evaluation with specific exams for each part. If all required minimums are not met, the final grade will be 'Fail' with a maximum of 4.0. Resits for practicals can involve retaking only the failed parts, and the CAM programming test must be taken individually if the teamwork grade is below 5/10.
